$comment: The canonical schema is schema/profile.schema.json. daemon/internal/profile/profile.schema.json is a byte-identical copy that go generate (task gen) writes; do not edit the copy.
title: padmate profile
description: Maps gamepad controls to keyboard shortcuts. Strict JSON: no comments and no trailing commas. The schema accepts what this padmate version can run; later versions only add optional properties, so a valid profile stays valid.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, so that editors validate and complete the file. padmate ignores it.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the profile format, frozen as 1. A file of version 0 (the previews before the freeze) has the same format: padmate reads it as version 1 without rewriting it, and a file of a newer version is refused.

extends.description: Library ID of the profile this one builds on (ADR-0070). Only a profile of the library can have it. What this profile does not write is taken from that profile: a layer's control, a function key's control, a timing, analog or feedback setting, the default layer and the script. A control written here replaces the whole control of the parent. The chain may have up to 4 parents, and a loop is an error.

defaultLayer.description: The base layer name active at startup.

controlNames.description: User-visible names for canonical controls; separate from binding action labels.

analog.description: Analog stick, d-pad and half-axis recognizer settings.

feedback.description: Basic controller feedback for layer changes and pause state.

script.description: Optional TypeScript script runtime for this profile.

base.description: The base layer, active whenever no other layer is.

functionKeys.description: The old format of the function key bindings (ADR-0069), still valid: the sets of back (View, Create, Share, Minus) and start (Menu, Options, Plus). Without functionSet, the set used is start's, plus back's for the controls start's does not bind. Optional; write functionSet instead. The sets cannot bind back or start.

functionSet.description: Bindings that apply while the function key is held (ADR-0075, MAP-27). The function key is one for every profile, chosen in config.json (functionKey: start by default, back or guide). A control that the set does not bind keeps its normal binding. Optional. When both functionSet and functionKeys are written, functionKeys is ignored.

script.title: Script runtime
script.description: TypeScript script entry point and host API version.

entry.description: Entry file relative to the profile directory.

api.description: Script host API version. The values are the versions this daemon supports: the current one and the previous 0.N (docs/SCRIPTING.md).

params.description: Script parameter values, validated against the script's parameter declarations.

tickHz.description: Continuous input and onTick sampling frequency. Missed ticks are skipped.

analog.title: Analog settings
analog.description: Dead zones, direction modes and d-pad conversion.

mode.description: Direction mode. knob turns the stick into a virtual knob: it emits no directions, and every knobStepDeg degrees of rotation gives one ls.cw or ls.ccw (rs.cw, rs.ccw) tick. mouse makes the stick move the mouse pointer (mouseSpeed, curve, mouseSmoothingMs): it emits no directions either, and no knob ticks; ls.active, ls.inner and ls.outer still work. The pointer starts as soon as the stick leaves the deadzone: directionThreshold does not hold it back.

deadzone.description: Radial deadzone as a fraction of travel.

directionThreshold.description: Normalized magnitude needed to emit a direction (and to press ls.active, rs.active). It does not hold back the pointer of a stick in mode mouse, which moves as soon as the stick leaves the deadzone.

outerThreshold.description: Normalized magnitude at which the stick enters its outer ring (ls.outer, rs.outer). Below it, while the stick is active, it is in the inner ring (ls.inner, rs.inner). Measured like directionThreshold, after deadzone and saturation. It leaves the outer ring 0.05 below this value.

diagonalWidth.description: Width of diagonal sectors in degrees.

directionDelayMs.description: Delay before committing a direction change.

diagonalFallback.description: Fallback when an eight-way diagonal is unbound.

knobStepDeg.description: Rotation in degrees that gives one knob tick when mode is knob.

knobTick.description: Give the controller a short tick (the tick haptic) for each knob step that sends a key, when mode is knob. Steps of a direction nothing binds make none, and a binding of ls.cw, ls.ccw, rs.cw or rs.ccw that sets its own haptic plays that one instead. It follows feedback.rumble and feedback.strength like every haptic. Without mode knob it does nothing.

label.description: What the editor calls the stick's movement on its controller label (the press of the stick is labelled by the label of its leftstick or rightstick binding). The daemon does not use it.

curve.description: Response curve of the push depth. It shapes the rate of a repeat that sets minRateHz (a repeat on ls.up, ls.active, ls.outer and the like) and, in mode mouse, the pointer speed (mouseSpeed times the curve of the depth). The depth of a repeat is 0 at directionThreshold and 1 at full travel; the depth of the pointer is 0 at the edge of the deadzone and 1 at saturation (directionThreshold does not matter to it). Linear uses the depth as it is, quadratic squares it, cubic cubes it. No threshold moves, and script values are not changed.

mouseSpeed.description: Pointer speed in mode mouse at full travel, in mouse movement units per second (the system scales them with its pointer speed). The speed follows the push: mouseSpeed times the curve of the depth, where the depth is 0 at the edge of the deadzone and 1 at saturation, so the pointer moves as soon as the stick leaves the deadzone.

mouseSmoothingMs.description: Smoothing of the pointer in mode mouse: the time constant, in milliseconds, of an exponential moving average of its velocity. 0 follows the stick at once; a larger value starts and stops the pointer more gently.

dpad.title: D-pad settings
dpad.description: Converts physical d-pad buttons to virtual directions.

fold.description: How four-way mode folds a diagonal.

trigger.title: Trigger thresholds
trigger.description: Trigger press and release hysteresis thresholds.

fullPress.description: Second-stage press threshold: at or above this fraction of its travel the trigger also presses lt.full or rt.full. It must be greater than press.

fullRelease.description: Second-stage release threshold: at or below this fraction lt.full or rt.full goes up again. It must not exceed fullPress.

curve.description: Response curve of the pull depth, used only for the rate of a repeat that sets minRateHz (a repeat on lt, lt.full and the like). The depth is 0 at the press threshold (fullPress for lt.full) and 1 at full travel; linear uses it as it is, quadratic squares it, cubic cubes it. No threshold moves, and script values are not changed.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.description: Controller feedback: the times, strength and pause color of the pulses and lights. The switches rumble, led, pause and lowBattery are no longer read: they are global settings in config.json feedback (ADR-0067). Files that have them stay valid.

rumble.description: No longer read (ADR-0067): the rumble switch is config.json feedback.rumble. Accepted so that older files load; do not write it.

led.description: No longer read (ADR-0067): the lights switch is config.json feedback.led. Accepted so that older files load; do not write it.

pause.description: No longer read (ADR-0067): the pause alert switch is config.json feedback.pause. Accepted so that older files load; do not write it.

lowBattery.description: No longer read (ADR-0067): the low-battery alert switch is config.json feedback.lowBattery. Accepted so that older files load; do not write it.

shortMs.description: Duration of each non-base mode pulse in milliseconds.

longMs.description: Duration of the pulse when returning to base, in milliseconds.

strength.description: Low and high rumble strength from 0 through 65535.

pausedColor.description: RGB LED color used while mapping is paused.

layer.title: Layer
layer.description: Bindings of one layer, keyed by control. Control names describe where a control sits, not what is printed on it, so a profile works the same on Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo pads. The Xbox style names a, b, x, y, lb, rb, l3, r3 and select are aliases; bind each control only once.

color.description: Optional feedback color for this layer.

south.description: Bottom face button: A (Xbox), Cross (PlayStation), B (Nintendo).

east.description: Right face button: B (Xbox), Circle (PlayStation), A (Nintendo).

west.description: Left face button: X (Xbox), Square (PlayStation), Y (Nintendo).

north.description: Top face button: Y (Xbox), Triangle (PlayStation), X (Nintendo).

back.description: Left center button: View or Back (Xbox), Create, Share or Select (PlayStation), Minus (Nintendo). Ignored while it is the function key (config.json functionKey, ADR-0075): then it sends nothing and cannot be bound.

guide.description: Center logo button: Xbox button, PS button, Home (Nintendo). Windows or Steam may also react to it. Ignored while it is the function key (config.json functionKey, ADR-0075).

start.description: Right center button: Menu or Start (Xbox), Options or Start (PlayStation), Plus (Nintendo). Ignored while it is the function key (config.json functionKey, ADR-0075), which it is by default: then it sends nothing and cannot be bound.

leftshoulder.description: Left shoulder button: LB (Xbox), L1 (PlayStation), L (Nintendo).

rightshoulder.description: Right shoulder button: RB (Xbox), R1 (PlayStation), R (Nintendo).

misc1.description: Extra button: Share (Xbox Series), Microphone (PlayStation 5), Capture (Nintendo Switch Pro).

misc2.description: Extra button 2, on pads that have one. Which button it is depends on the pad; padmatectl monitor shows the name.

misc3.description: Extra button 3, on pads that have one, such as the GameCube left trigger click.

misc4.description: Extra button 4, on pads that have one, such as the GameCube right trigger click.

misc5.description: Extra button 5, on pads that have one. Which button it is depends on the pad; padmatectl monitor shows the name.

misc6.description: Extra button 6, on pads that have one. Which button it is depends on the pad; padmatectl monitor shows the name.

paddle1.description: Upper back paddle under the right hand: P1 (Xbox Elite), right back button (DualSense Edge).

paddle2.description: Upper back paddle under the left hand: P3 (Xbox Elite), left back button (DualSense Edge).

paddle3.description: Lower back paddle under the right hand: P2 (Xbox Elite), right Fn button (DualSense Edge).

paddle4.description: Lower back paddle under the left hand: P4 (Xbox Elite), left Fn button (DualSense Edge).

lt.description: Left trigger as a button: LT (Xbox), L2 (PlayStation), ZL (Nintendo). It goes down at 30% of its travel and up again below 20%.

rt.description: Right trigger as a button: RT (Xbox), R2 (PlayStation), ZR (Nintendo). It goes down at 30% of its travel and up again below 20%.

ls.active.description: Left stick pushed beyond its active threshold.

rs.active.description: Right stick pushed beyond its active threshold.

ls.inner.description: Left stick pushed past its active threshold but not into the outer ring. Down together with ls.active and the direction controls.

ls.outer.description: Left stick pushed into its outer ring (analog.ls.outerThreshold). Down together with ls.active and the direction controls.

ls.cw.description: One clockwise tick of the left stick used as a knob (analog.ls.mode knob). It goes down and up at once.

ls.ccw.description: One counter-clockwise tick of the left stick used as a knob (analog.ls.mode knob). It goes down and up at once.

rs.inner.description: Right stick pushed past its active threshold but not into the outer ring. Down together with rs.active and the direction controls.

rs.outer.description: Right stick pushed into its outer ring (analog.rs.outerThreshold). Down together with rs.active and the direction controls.

rs.cw.description: One clockwise tick of the right stick used as a knob (analog.rs.mode knob). It goes down and up at once.

rs.ccw.description: One counter-clockwise tick of the right stick used as a knob (analog.rs.mode knob). It goes down and up at once.

lt.full.description: Left trigger second stage: down from analog.lt.fullPress (90% of its travel) until analog.lt.fullRelease (80%). lt stays down while it is.

rt.full.description: Right trigger second stage: down from analog.rt.fullPress (90% of its travel) until analog.rt.fullRelease (80%). rt stays down while it is.

functionKeys.title: Function keys
functionKeys.description: The old format of the function key bindings (ADR-0069): the sets of View (back) and Menu (start). Still valid; functionSet (ADR-0075) replaces it. Each set is written like a layer.

back.description: Bindings used while back is held: View (Xbox), Create, Share or Select (PlayStation), Minus (Nintendo).

start.description: Bindings used while start is held: Menu or Start (Xbox), Options or Start (PlayStation), Plus (Nintendo).

functionSet.title: Function key set
functionSet.description: Bindings used while one function key is held, keyed by control and written like a layer without a color: the same bindings, gestures and actions. A control the set does not bind keeps its normal binding. back and start (and the alias select) cannot be bound here: they are the function keys themselves. Bind each control only once.

binding.title: Binding
binding.description: What one control does: an optional label and the action for each gesture. Only press exists for now; a binding without an action does nothing.

block.description: Consume the control in this layer without producing an action.

label.description: Short name of what the binding does, shown by the UI, the HUD, the cheat sheet and dry-run output. It does not change the behavior.

press.description: Action that starts when the control goes down.

release.description: Action that runs when the control goes up.

tap.description: Action for a tap, when no hold or later tap follows.

doubleTap.description: Action for the second tap in a double tap.

tripleTap.description: Action for the third tap in a triple tap.

quadTap.description: Action for the fourth tap in a quad tap.

hold.description: Action after the hold threshold is reached.

policy.description: How a tap and hold interaction is resolved.

latch.description: Keep a hold action until the next press of this control.

haptic.description: A short haptic on the controller each time a gesture of this binding runs: tick is one crisp click, confirm two short pulses, error one long low pulse, pulse1 to pulse4 that many pulses. It plays once per dispatch, not on each repeat of a held key, never for a block binding, and not when feedback.rumble is false or feedback.strength is 0. It never interrupts the layer or pause pulses.

action.title: Action
action.description: What a gesture does. The type property selects the kind of action; "keys" presses a keyboard shortcut.

steps.description: The steps of a sequence action, in order: 1 to 64 of them.

text.description: The text of a text action: 1 to 256 UTF-16 code units, typed a character at a time; a newline is an Enter tap and a tab a Tab tap; no other control character.

file.description: Macro file name in the profile's macros folder.

op.description: Layer operation (hold, toggle, switch, cycle), mouse operation (precision, jump) or HUD operation (hints); layerAction, mouseAction and hudAction list them.

factor.description: Speed factor of a mouse precision action.

x.description: Horizontal position of a mouse jump action, as a fraction of the virtual desktop.

y.description: Vertical position of a mouse jump action, as a fraction of the virtual desktop.

mouseAction.title: Mouse action
mouseAction.description: Changes how the mouse pointer moves. precision slows the pointer: while the gesture is held (press or hold), every stick of the slot in mode mouse moves at factor times its speed, and the smallest factor of the precision actions held wins. jump puts the pointer at x and y, fractions of the virtual desktop, once when the gesture fires.

op.description: precision slows the pointer while the gesture is held; jump puts it somewhere.

factor.description: precision: the fraction of its speed the pointer keeps while the gesture is held, from 0.05 to 1 (default 0.3).

x.description: jump: the horizontal position as a fraction of the virtual desktop, 0 (left edge) to 1 (right edge).

y.description: jump: the vertical position as a fraction of the virtual desktop, 0 (top edge) to 1 (bottom edge).

hudAction.title: HUD action
hudAction.description: Controls the overlay (the HUD). hints shows the labels of the bindings of the current layer stack while the gesture is held (press or hold); it presses no key and moves nothing. The overlay is an optional part of the UI: without it the action does nothing.

op.description: hints shows the key hints while the gesture is held.

sequenceAction.title: Sequence action
sequenceAction.description: Runs steps one after the other when the gesture fires: tap a shortcut, wait, or type a text. It holds nothing, so it works on every gesture, and takes no mode or repeat. A shortcut is tapped as in a list of keys; a wait counts from the release of the step before it; a text is typed a character at a time, tapGapMs apart. A second trigger runs after the first is over. Releasing everything (pause, reload, a change of profile) cancels what is left.

steps.description: The steps, in order: 1 to 64 of them. Each is {"keys": shortcut}, {"wait": milliseconds} or {"text": text}.

textAction.title: Text action
textAction.description: Types a text when the gesture fires, a character at a time, tapGapMs apart (20 ms unless set). It uses the Unicode input of Windows, so the keyboard layout and the input method play no part and Chinese comes out as written. It holds nothing, so it works on every gesture, and takes no mode or repeat. A second trigger types after the first is done.

text.description: The text: 1 to 256 UTF-16 code units (a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as an emoji, is two). A newline (\n) is typed as an Enter tap and a tab (\t) as a Tab tap; any other control character is refused.

sequenceStep.title: Sequence step
sequenceStep.description: One step of a sequence action: tap a shortcut (keys), wait (wait, in milliseconds) or type a text (text). A step has exactly one of the three.

keys.description: Tap this shortcut, written as in a keys action ("Ctrl+A"), for tapPressMs; the next step starts tapGapMs after it is released.

wait.description: Wait this many milliseconds, 1 to 10000, counted from the release of the step before it (from the start, for the first step). Waits one after another add up; tapGapMs is the least time between two steps.

text.description: Type this text, as a text action does.

profileAction.title: Profile action
profileAction.description: Requests a switch to another library profile without blocking input.

profile.description: Target library ID; lowercase letters, digits, dash or underscore.

macroAction.title: Macro action
macroAction.description: Runs a macro once: a TypeScript or JavaScript file in the profile's macros folder whose default export is a function.

file.description: The macro's file name in the macros folder, such as "复制全部.ts": a name of 1 to 40 characters and a lowercase .ts or .js extension.

scriptAction.title: Script action
scriptAction.description: Invokes a named action registered by the profile's TypeScript script.

args.description: Named argument values, checked and clamped by the host.

type.description: Kind of action: "keys" presses a keyboard shortcut.

keys.description: The shortcut: modifiers and one key joined by "+", such as "Ctrl+Shift+Z", "F13" or "Space". Names are case-insensitive. Modifiers are Ctrl, Shift, Alt and Win, or sided: LCtrl, RCtrl, LShift, RShift, LAlt, RAlt, LWin, RWin. A letter, digit or punctuation character names the key that types it (write Plus for +); KeyZ, Key1 and so on name a fixed position on the US layout; sc:0x2C sends a raw scan code. Named keys include F1 to F24, Esc, Tab, Enter, Backspace, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown and the arrows Up, Down, Left, Right; padmatectl keys list shows them all. The mouse wheel is a key too: WheelUp, WheelDown, WheelLeft and WheelRight turn the wheel one notch when pressed, once per press and with nothing on release, and can follow modifiers, as in Ctrl+WheelUp. The mouse buttons are keys too: MouseLeft, MouseRight, MouseMiddle, MouseX1 and MouseX2 (also LButton, RButton, MButton, XButton1 and XButton2) go down and up like keys, so Shift+MouseLeft clicks with Shift down; a held button is never pressed again, so a repeat on a button needs mode "tap" (repeated clicks) and typematic repeat is rejected.

mode.description: "hold" keeps the shortcut down; "tap" sends complete taps. The gesture chooses the default, or repeat.style="tap" chooses tap when mode is omitted.

repeat.description: Optional repeat while the control is held; style follows mode by default.

repeat.title: Repeat
repeat.description: Repeat timing for a held action.

style.description: typematic uses hold mode; tap sends complete taps and uses tap mode.

delayMs.description: Delay before the first repeat; zero starts at the first repeat period.

rateHz.description: Repeat rate in repeats per second (default 12). With minRateHz it is the rate at full travel.

minRateHz.description: Makes the repeat rate follow how far the control is pushed: minRateHz at the control's activation threshold, rateHz at full travel, shaped by the stick's or trigger's curve. Only for stick, trigger and half-axis controls. It must not exceed rateHz. The delay before the first repeat is not changed, and the rate is still capped by the same-key maximum (tapPressMs + tapGapMs).
